_note: Single source of truth for the Reading and Writing section. Read by pipeline/validate.py, pipeline/build_packs.py and the app (copied into app/assets/data).
title: Reading and Writing

words_in_context.name: Words in Context
stems: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
As used in the text, what does the word "{word}" most nearly mean?

text_structure_purpose.name: Text Structure and Purpose
stems: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

cross_text.name: Cross-Text Connections
stems: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the {claim} in Text 1?
Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

central_ideas.name: Central Ideas and Details
stems: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
According to the text, {detail question}?
Based on the text, {detail question}?

coe_textual.name: Command of Evidence (Textual)
stems: Which finding, if true, would most directly support {the claim}?
Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken {the claim}?
Which quotation from {the work} most effectively illustrates the claim?

coe_quantitative.name: Command of Evidence (Quantitative)
stems: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the {example/statement}?
Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the {example/statement}?
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support {the claim}?
Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support {the claim}?

inferences.name: Inferences
stems: Which choice most logically completes the text?

boundaries.name: Boundaries
stems: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

form_structure_sense.name: Form, Structure, and Sense
stems: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

transitions.name: Transitions
stems: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

rhetorical_synthesis.name: Rhetorical Synthesis
stems: The student wants to {goal}. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

traps.too_broad: Too broad: claims more than the text supports
traps.too_narrow: Too narrow: a detail, not the whole point
traps.not_in_text: Not in the text: brings in an idea the text never states
traps.reversed: Reversed: flips the relationship or the author's view
traps.true_irrelevant: True but irrelevant: accurate, but does not answer the question
traps.wrong_tone: Wrong tone or shade: a near-synonym that does not fit the context
traps.wrong_logic: Wrong logic: the wrong relationship between ideas
traps.misses_goal: Misses the goal: uses the notes but not for the stated purpose
traps.grammar_rule: Grammar rule broken: does not follow Standard English conventions
